seo.title: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Ascot | Fit-Only Installation | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: The bathroom brands we fit in Ascot, and how our fit-only installation model works — your products, our labour, from Geberit and hansgrohe to Victoria + Albert.

h1: Bathroom brands we fit in Ascot

hero.intro: We work on a fit-only basis across Ascot, which means we install the bathroom products you've already chosen — from a showroom, a designer's specification, or your own research — rather than selling you a fixed catalogue of our own. For homeowners in Ascot's larger detached and executive-style properties, that distinction matters, because the brands that get specified here tend to sit at the more considered end of the market, and getting the installation detail right on those products is a different job to a standard retail fit. Across the projects we work on, a recurring set of brands turns up again and again, and we've built our fitting process around the specific detail each one needs, rather than treating every bathroom brand as interchangeable once it's out of the box.

sections.heading: The fit-only model, explained
sections.body: Fit-only means exactly what it says: the labour and installation expertise, without us also supplying or marking up the products. You choose your sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and fittings through whichever route suits you — a bathroom showroom, an online retailer, a designer's specification, or a brand's own stockist — and we fit them to the standard they're designed for. This works particularly well in Ascot, where a lot of the specification has already been through a designer or a showroom consultation before we're brought in at survey stage. It also means the quote you get reflects labour and fitting complexity honestly, rather than bundling in a retail margin on the products themselves. Where it matters most is in the detail: a concealed cistern frame, a frameless glass screen, or a textured brassware finish all need to be fitted correctly for that specific product, and we work through exactly what's been specified before a wall closes up or a screen goes in.

sections.heading: Brands we fit
sections.body: Geberit concealed cisterns, wall-hung WCs and AquaClean shower toilets are among the sanitaryware we fit most often — correct frame selection and structural fixing matter more here than with most brands, because the cistern and pan weight sit entirely on the carrier frame rather than the wall tiles. We also regularly fit Villeroy & Boch and Duravit sanitaryware, including Duravit's SensoWash and V&B's ViClean shower toilet seats, where confirming the right flush plate, pan and frame generation — or the correct installation route between a brand's own frame and a standard concealed cistern — is settled before anything is ordered, not discovered on fitting day. On the brassware side, hansgrohe and GROHE cover a wide span of the work we do, from thermostatic shower valves and mixer taps through to Rapid SL cistern frames and digital shower products, while AXOR and Dornbracht turn up on more design-led specifications where a brushed or matte black finish shows every mark from a careless fit in a way chrome never does — handling and sequencing matter as much as the plumbing itself. For baths and shower trays, Kaldewei's titanium-enamelled steel needs even, accurate bearing across the full base rather than the flex-prevention an acrylic bath support relies on, and Victoria + Albert's cast volcanic limestone-and-resin baths carry genuine weight that has to be planned for in the access route and floor loading before the bath even leaves the showroom. We've fitted all of these, and the specific installation detail each one needs, across projects in and around Ascot.

sections.heading: Why the fitting detail matters more at this specification level
sections.body: At the specification level common in Ascot's larger properties, the margin for error on installation detail tends to be smaller, not larger. A scuff on a brushed Dornbracht finish or a Laufen basin with its noticeably finer SaphirKeramik rim is far more visible — and far more expensive to put right — than the same mistake on a standard mid-range product. That's part of why we work through exactly what's been specified at survey, confirm the installation route for frames, fixings and finishes before any wall or floor is closed up, and sequence the fit so that delicate or design-led products aren't handled more than they need to be. The product choice is yours; getting it fitted properly, once it's chosen, is ours.

faqs.q: Do I have to buy my bathroom products from you?
faqs.a: No. We work fit-only, which means you choose and supply your own sanitaryware, brassware and tiles — through a showroom, designer or retailer — and we handle the installation to the standard those products need.

faqs.q: Which bathroom brands do you fit most often in Ascot?
faqs.a: Geberit, Villeroy & Boch and Duravit sanitaryware, and hansgrohe and GROHE brassware, come up most frequently. We also regularly fit more design-led brands such as AXOR, Dornbracht, Kaldewei and Victoria + Albert.

faqs.q: Can you fit a brand that isn't listed here?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes — we work through the specific installation requirements of whatever's been specified at survey stage. If a product has an unusual fixing or frame requirement, we confirm it before anything is ordered rather than discovering it on fitting day.

faqs.q: Why does the brand of brassware or sanitaryware affect the fitting cost?
faqs.a: Different brands have different fixing systems, frame compatibility and finish sensitivity. A brushed or matte black finish, for example, shows marks from careless handling far more than chrome, so some products need more careful sequencing and handling than others.

faqs.q: Do you work with Ascot bathroom showrooms and designers?
faqs.a: Yes. A lot of the specification we fit in Ascot has already been through a showroom consultation or designer before we're brought in at survey stage, and we're used to working from an existing specification rather than starting from scratch.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Ascot brands-in-area page, implying brand and material choice through a close vanity fixture detail rather than a full room shot. Subject and action: a close-to-mid shot of a wall-mounted basin with a single-lever brassware mixer tap, water droplets caught mid-settle on the basin surface from a recently finished test run, no motion. Setting and work-stage: a finished bathroom vanity area in a contemporary extension to an Ascot executive-style house, daytime, bright but not harsh natural light from an unseen side window. Composition: tight three-quarter angle focused on the basin and tap, tiled wall and a sliver of mirror edge visible in the soft-focus background, tap and basin rim sharply in focus in the foreground. Light and materials: Calacatta marble-effect porcelain splashback tile, matte black single-lever brassware, bright directional daylight from one side casting a defined but soft-edged shadow of the tap across the basin, minor water spotting on the tap body consistent with recent use. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on fixtures, no LED strip lighting anywhere in frame, no twin symmetrical basins, no uniform gold colour wash, no plants, florals or candles as props, no water shown actively running, varied and believable sheen on the marble-effect tile with faint, realistic water spotting rather than uniform gloss.
